       1             SENATOR FUSCHILLO:  Let me introduce my

      11      here today to offer testimony to the Committee.

      12             We know how busy you are, and we appreciate

      13      you taking time out of your schedule to be here.

      14             The MTA, as we know, is the largest

      15      transportation system in North America.

      16             It covers -- its area -- its service area

      17      covers of over 5,000 square miles.

      18             Its transit systems have an annual ridership

      19      of over 2.6 billion, and its bridges and tunnels

      20      serve more than 280 million vehicles a year.

      21             The operations are funded through a more than

      22      $13 million budget.

      23             The MTA has many longstanding issues with its

      24      finances.

      25             Fares have risen dramatically over the past





 

                                                                  4
       1      years, making MTA increasingly unaffordable for some

       2      of its passengers.

       3             Riders are paying 47 percent more for a metro

       4      card, more than 30 percent more for a commuter-rail

       5      ticket, and more than 30 percent more to use the

       6      bridges and tunnels than we were in 2007.

       7             These increases are far above the rate of

       8      inflation.

       9             Over the years, there have been numerous

      10      cases of waste, fraud, and abuse, along with

      11      questionable spending practices, which have cost the

      12      Authority and ratepayers significantly.

      13             The good news is, under new Chairman and

      14      CEO Tom Prendergast, MTA's financial picture is

      15      improving.

      16             New York State delivered over $4 billion in

      17      operating aid to the MTA this year, an increase of

      18      over 10 percent from last year.

      19             The MTA has instituted many cost-cutting

      20      measures which have resulted in hundreds of millions

      21      of dollars, and when combined with additional

      22      State aid and increasing revenue, it has eliminated

      23      its 2014 budget gap and currently reduced out-year

      24      budget gaps; however, numerous challenges remain for

      25      the MTA.





 

                                                                  5
       1             It is still recovering from enormous damage

       2      caused by "Superstorm Sandy."

       3             It has significant infrastructure needs and

       4      must formulate a new capital plan to meet those

       5      needs, and is facing substantial increases in debt

       6      service and fringe-benefit costs.

       7             The purpose of today's hearing is to get a

       8      detailed update from the MTA leadership on the

       9      state's Authority's finances, how it plans to spend

      10      ratepayers' money, through its capital and operating

      11      budget, and what steps it will take to reduce costs,

      12      improve services, and continually try to strive to

      13      make it more affordable for its riders.

      15      testimony from Chairman and CEO Tom Prendergast, as

      17      Metro-North, New York City Transit, MTA Bridges &

      22      opportunity to being here.

      24      Ranking Member of the Transportation Committee.

      18      presentation of the July financial plan to the

       1      be, quote/unquote, much improved.

       2             And, overall, we're pleased that it

       3      recognized we're on track to cut $1.3 billion out of

       4      our annual operating budget.

       5             I'll talk more in a moment about both our

       6      financial plan and our unprecedented cost-cutting,

       7      but first of all, I would like to set the stage a

       8      little with some basic facts about how -- the MTA

       9      and how we're funded.

      10             Every day, the MTA moves 8 1/2 million people

      11      on our subways, buses, Metro-North, and

      12      Long Island Railroad.

      13             We're one of the few transportation systems

      14      in the world that still operates 24 hours a day,

      15      7 days a week, and our 7 bridges and tunnels carry

      16      nearly 300 million vehicles a year.

      17             When you put it all together, with a

      18      lifeblood of a $1.4 trillion economy, second only to

      19      the city and the region of Tokyo, Japan, and we make

      20      up 11 -- this economy makes up 11 percent of the

      21      nation's gross domestic product, but providing this

      22      service is not cheap.

      23             It costs $13.2 billion a year, and like every

      24      transit network in the country, fares cover only a

      25      portion of the costs needed to run the system.

       1             In our case, just over half our costs are

       2      covered by fares and tolls across the system, and

       3      total fare revenue this year is projected to be

       4      about $5.5 billion.

       5             When you subtract that from our operating

       6      expenses, you're left with a difference of about

       7      $7.7 billion.

       9      single day:

      10             How do we make up that difference?

      13      about $1 billion.

      19      and local subsidies, dedicated taxes, and other

      20      fluctuating revenue services that make up that

      22             Today the problems with this model are clear.

      23             Revenues based on tax receipts vary with the

      24      economy and can leave us with significant operating

      25      deficits.

       1             The cost of running our operation is

       1      truth is, despite what some people have said, we

       1             We're using $80 million in surplus

       1      go a long time in between them.

       1      speaks to the value we provide.
